What the 3,543 records actually are

The count flatters the data. Just under half the records are sub-0.2-hectare fragments — an entrance, a trailhead, a bird sanctuary, a rose garden — sitting inside a larger park that is also its own record. Griffith Park is the 17.4 km² polygon and also the Observatory, Fern Dell Hiking Trail, Commonwealth Entrance and several 69 m² slivers.

Any per-park number has to collapse records to a park entity first, using PARENT_PLACEKEY, area and polygon containment. Counting rows counts entrances.

Records can carry more than one flag. Known bad rows the flags catch: Westfield Playtown (a mall filed as a park), Hollywood Walk of Fame and Beverly Hills Sign (landmarks on SafeGraph's default box), and Maluaka Beach Maui, which is geocoded into LA County. A name that does not match its coordinates cannot be caught automatically — check names before publishing anything park-by-park.

Joining the county and city vehicle counts

What to plan for when the agency data arrives.

  • Match on name plus street address, then confirm by point-in-polygon. STREET_ADDRESS is populated on all 3,543 records and LOCATION_NAME follows agency naming closely — "Algin Sutton Recreation Center", "Franklin D Roosevelt Park". Name alone is not enough: agency rosters carry one row per park, SafeGraph carries one per feature.
  • A vehicle count is a parking-lot count, so prefer the 717 parks whose polygon includes the lot. INCLUDES_PARKING_LOT is only 60% populated (717 true, 1,712 false, 1,114 unknown). Where the polygon excludes the lot, device visits and vehicle entries are measuring adjacent ground and will not move together.
  • Expect a jurisdiction split the data does not label. SafeGraph has no owner field, so county, city, state, federal and private parks sit in one pile. The city flag here is derived from the CDTFA boundary via the park's tract, not a vendor city name. A county roster and a city roster will each match a different subset.
  • Vehicle counts would fix the real weakness. Agency counts are a census of arrivals at a known gate, not a ~6% device sample with a shifting panel — which is exactly what the section below could not overcome. They are the better measure, and they can validate the device series where both exist.
  • Carry the keys. PLACEKEY is the join key across SafeGraph and Veraset; SAFEGRAPH_PLACE_ID and STORE_ID are also in the inventory for older SafeGraph deliveries.

What the visit data can and cannot say about the raids

Tested on the 431 City of LA parks with near-complete coverage, 14 weeks before 6 June against the 4 weeks after. The honest answer is that it finds nothing, and that its pre-trends are too severe to trust either way.

Why the earlier drop was not real

The Veraset feed grew about 14× across the window — 584 visits per park in the week of 1 March, 8,037 by 27 June, across a stable set of 431 parks. Any raw before-and-after comparison measures the feed being built out.

Counting the panel's own devices by home tract settles which comparisons survive it:

GroupPanel growth, May → Jun/Jul
Within 3 mi of a site4.72×
Beyond 3 mi4.78×
70%+ Latino tracts4.75×
70%+ non-Latino White tracts5.43×
  • Distance holds up. The panel grew within 1% of evenly, so a near-versus-far design is not contaminated — and it shows no effect.
  • The Latino comparison does not. The panel grew 12.5% less in Latino tracts, which is larger than the 4% gap in raw park visits that first looked like a decline. Correct for it and the sign flips.
  • Pre-trends fail the test regardless. Treated and control parks were already on significantly different paths in March, converging toward zero before 6 June and then staying flat. There is no break at the raids.

So: no measurable park-visit decline attributable to the June 2025 raids in this data, and the design cannot support a claim in either direction. That is a limit of a 6% device panel that doubled mid-study, not evidence that nothing happened. Gate counts from the agencies are the way past it.

Other recreation categories, for reference

Parks are NAICS 712190 and nothing else — SafeGraph's category tags are no help, since the 2,586 LA places tagged park-ish are garden centres and hardware stores. These neighbouring codes are separate universes.

Advan Weekly Patterns+, the panel the rest of this project runs on, carries 14 of these 3,543 parks — all national forests. Advan builds its universe from business polygons, so free public parks are out of scope. That is why park work needs SafeGraph Places for the roster and Veraset for the visits.

Park roster and polygons: SafeGraph Global Places (POI) & Geometry via Dewey, NAICS 712190, LA County by exact point-in-tract against 2020 tracts. Visits: Veraset Visits, daily, aggregated to park × day with cells under 5 visits suppressed; no device identifiers were ever requested. Neighbourhood classes from ACS 2018–2022. Enforcement sites are the nine cost-of-fear sites, event window anchored to 6 June 2025. Built from park_inventory.csv · 3,543 records × 38 columns.
